construct: NO CONSTRUCT, AND NOT RECOMBINANT -- WHICH CUTS BOTH WAYS. Native protein: defatted soybean flour -> soybean protein isolate -> glycinin fraction (pH 4.8 precipitation) -> dissociated into acidic (glycinin-A) and basic (glycinin-B) subunits by 90 C / 30 min in 30 mM Tris-HCl, 15 mM beta-mercaptoethanol, pH 8.0, then pH precipitation, dialysis (MWCO 3.5 kDa), lyophilisation. Fibrillisation: "Protein solutions (20 mg mL-1, pH 2.0) were heated at 90 C for 12 h under constant magnetic stirring (500 rpm)". || THREE CONSTRUCT CAVEATS, ALL MATERIAL. (1) THE STARTING MATERIAL IS A MIXTURE, NOT A PROTEIN. "glycinin-A" is the pooled acidic subunits of at least five glycinin gene products (G1-G5); the paper reports ">90% purity" of the FRACTION, which is a statement about the absence of other soy proteins, not about which glycinin gene is in it. (2) THE FIBRIL-FORMING SPECIES WAS NEVER WEIGHED OR SEQUENCED. SDS-PAGE was run on the starting fractions (Figure 1a) and NOT on the fibrils; there is no mass spectrometry anywhere in the paper -- grep of the full text returns 0 hits for "mass spec" and 0 for "hydroly". So whether the fibrils contain intact acidic subunit or chain fragments is not addressed. 12 h at pH 2.0 and 90 C is a condition under which acid hydrolysis of the backbone would be expected, and for other food proteins fibrillation under exactly this protocol is reported to proceed via hydrolysis-generated peptides -- BUT THAT IS BACKGROUND, NOT A SOURCE OPENED HERE, and is recorded as an open question, not as a finding. frame: 704-residue canonical UniProt Q9VSR3 (ORB2_DROME), which IS the Orb2B frame. VERIFIED AGAINST THE SEQUENCE, not assumed: UniProt 176-206 returns QLHQQQHQQQHQQHQQHQQQQQLHQHQQQLS, which matches the paper's Figure 4F sequence character for character, and the 704 aa length matches the 704 printed for Orb2B in that figure. THE FRAME TRAP IS REAL AND WAS CHECKED: Orb2A and Orb2B share the prion-like domain but differ in their N-terminal extension (Orb2A 9 residues, Orb2B 162; Orb2A is 551 aa), so the same core carries different residue numbers in the two isoforms. The canonical entry is the long one, so no conversion is needed.
evidence: Cryo-EM of amyloid filaments purified from approximately three million adult Drosophila heads, 2.6 A overall resolution, atomic model built DE NOVO from density. VERBATIM: 'the protofilament core structure extends from residues 176-206 of Orb2B'. Three identical protofilaments, C3 symmetry, triangular cross-section ~80 A per side with a 15 A channel; twist -1.55 deg, rise 4.75 A. The fold is a hairpin of beta1 (176-186) and beta2 (197-206) with a wide turn (187-196).
construct: ENDOGENOUS FULL-LENGTH PROTEIN FROM TISSUE -- the strongest construct provenance in this dataset. Purified from adult fly heads, 97.5% Orb2B by LC-MS/MS. NOT recombinant, and the distinction is the authors' own: 'When we assembled Orb2 filaments from recombinant protein, filaments were longer, morphologically distinct, less biochemically active, and had negligible seeding capacity compared to endogenous ones ... suggesting that the same prion-like protein can adopt distinct structures in vitro and in vivo.' A recombinant Orb2 row would therefore NOT be this row.
found_by: ORDERED CRYO-EM CORE, NOT A NECESSITY MAPPING. The region is the span resolved in the reconstruction; no deletion experiment establishes that 176-206 is required for aggregation. Route (a) under PREREGISTRATION 10b. NO PREDICTOR IS IN THE DISCOVERY PATH: the model was built de novo from density and stereochemically refined, and the paper names no aggregation predictor anywhere. Adjacent evidence that does NOT establish the range: Orb2 mutations known to disrupt aggregation map onto this interface (ref 10, Majumdar 2012), and removal of 54 residues from the glutamine-rich region impaired long-term but not short-term memory (ref 6, Keleman 2007) -- a memory readout over a different span, recorded so it is not mistaken for a mapping of 176-206.

The authors state the reason themselves -- 'wild-type beta2m is resistant to aggregation in vitro unless the protein is first unfolded by lowering the pH' -- and note that E44 and D76, which are buried in this core, 'will be protonated at the pH at which these fibrils were grown'.
